one_month_reasoning: No Synopsys earnings in the window: Q4 FY26 results are expected in early-to-mid December 2026, after 2026-10-31. Events inside the window: (1) Cadence Q3 2026 results, estimated for Oct 26 (date unconfirmed by the company), a sector read-across that could move SNPS by mid-single digits either way; (2) the FOMC on Oct 27-28, the first meeting after the Sept 16 hike to 3.75-4.00%, with the dot plot signalling one more 2026 hike. The 10-year yield averaged 4.99% in September, up from 4.12% a year earlier, so a hawkish surprise is a real downside risk for a ~26x software multiple; (3) the Nov 4 defendants' response in the Design IP class action falls just after the window, so it is not a factor; (4) analysts moving FY27 estimates up toward the $19.04-19.12 guide (BofA raised FY27 EPS by 7% and FY28 by 16%), and the ~$1B buyback starting. Short-horizon regularities pull in opposite directions: drift after a guidance surprise against a partial reversal of the ~18% two-session jump (415 to 490.54). Net: median at about spot ($491; I removed the small upward tilt from round 1 because of the FOMC risk), sigma ~12.3%, about the stock's usual monthly vol (45%/3.5 = 12.9%) less a little because no company print falls in the window, roughly symmetric in log terms.

fair_value.method: Blend of 23x FY28E non-GAAP EPS of $23.0 (=$529, 50%), a 3.8% FCF yield on FY28E FCF/share of $19.7 (=$518, 30%), and 28x SBC-burdened FY28E EPS of $18.45 (=$517, 20%). The FY28 figures are built from the Investor Day FY27 guide ($19.08 EPS, $3.1B FCF) haircut from the ~23% framework CAGR to ~20% growth; every multiple is cut about one turn from round 1 for a Fed that is hiking and a 10-year near 5%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28E non-GAAP EPS $23.0 x 23x NTM P/E (value as of Oct 2027, when FY28 is the forward year)

inputs_detail.derivation: $19.08 x 1.205. The framework's mid-20s EPS CAGR FY26-30 from $15.07 works out to ~23% a year (BofA computes 23% and raised its FY28 EPS 16% after the event, per 24/7 Wall St). FY27 alone is +26.6%, so I keep the ~20.5% FY28 haircut for slippage and the end of the Ansys cost-synergy tailwind. The rate hike does not cut EPS: the floating-rate term loans were fully repaid in Q1 FY26 and the remaining ~$10.1B is fixed-rate notes (10-Q Note 11), with ~$460M non-GAAP interest already in the guide.

SNPS trades at 25.7x the FY27 guide ($490.54/$19.08); CDNS at ~43x its 2026 guide ($350.73/$8.10) with 19% revenue growth vs SNPS ~15%. I keep a discount to CDNS for ~$6.4B net debt, the ~$5/share SBC gap and the IP history. Round 1 used 24x. I cut it to 23x because the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 with a 4.1% median dot for end-2026 and end-2027 (no cuts), and the 10-year averaged 4.99% in September vs 4.12% a year earlier (~+90bp). Higher discount rates weigh most on long-duration multiples. The stock's own de-rating from ~40x to ~26x forward over the past year happened alongside that rise in yields, so I do not assume it reverses. I don't go lower than 23x: the rate move is already partly in today's 25.7x, and roll-forward compression is the main reason the exit multiple sits below today's.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28E FCF $3.72B / 189M diluted shares = $19.7/share, valued at a 3.8% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: $3.1B x 1.20. The framework calls for mid-20s% FCF growth; I haircut it to 20%, as with EPS.

The FY27 guide is 190-192M and 191.6M were outstanding on 2026-08-24. The ~$1B buyback (about 2M shares at ~$500) and the policy of returning up to 50% of FCF offset SBC dilution, for a net ~1% drift down.

At $490.54 x 191M shares (~$93.7B), FY27 FCF of $3.1B is a 3.3% yield. Round 1 used 3.6% to account for ~$6.4B net debt ($10.04B less $3.61B cash, 10-Q). I add 0.2pt because the 10-year is now ~5.0-5.3%, so the FCF yield sits even further below the risk-free rate and needs more growth to justify it. Debt principal due is only ~$1.02B in each of FY27 and FY28 (10-Q schedule), so leverage is a valuation drag, not a funding risk.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: SBC-burdened P/E: FY28E non-GAAP EPS $23.0 less after-tax SBC $4.55 = $18.45 x 28x

inputs_detail.derivation: From the Investor Day GAAP-to-non-GAAP reconciliation
Shows the size of the non-GAAP add-backs (SBC plus Ansys amortization)
$970M x 1.08 growth = ~$1.05B, x (1-18% non-GAAP tax rate), / 189M shares

On SBC-burdened earnings, a ~23% EPS growth framework and a peer (CDNS) above 40x non-GAAP 2026 EPS support a high-20s multiple. I cut it by one turn from round 1's 29x for the rate backdrop, the same reasoning as the P/E leg. This method is mainly a cross-check that the non-GAAP P/E is not flattering the value.

bear.story: The FY27 guide proves aggressive, or rates keep rising. EDA and IP growth fade after the AI capex peak; agentic or open-source AI (the Kimi K3 episode cost SNPS 7.8% in a day) erodes seat-based pricing; China (9.9% of 9M FY26 revenue per the 10-Q) faces renewed export curbs; or the Design IP class action and a weak December print revive credibility doubts. With the Fed hiking toward 4.1% and the 10-year above 5%, FY28 EPS of ~$20.5 gets only ~17.5x, giving ~$355, just below the 52-week low.

base.story: Synopsys hits FY27 guidance (~$11.15B revenue, ~$19.1 EPS, $3.1B FCF) and guides FY28 to ~20% EPS growth. Deleveraging and the $1B buyback continue. Rates stay restrictive (no 2027 cuts), so the market holds ~23x NTM EPS of ~$23, giving ~$525-530.

bull.story: AI design complexity, the AWS $1B+ IP and EDA deal, Factory 2 royalties and GPT-Synopsys consumption revenue push growth above the framework. FY28 EPS reaches ~$24, inflation eases enough for the Fed to stop hiking, and the multiple re-rates toward ~28x, giving ~$680.

thesis_break_reason: $365 is ~19.1x the FY27 non-GAAP EPS guide and just above the 52-week low ($362.55), so it gives back the whole Investor Day re-rating and more. I lowered it from $375 because, with the Fed hiking and the 10-year at ~5%, a slide to ~19.5x on rates alone is now ordinary de-rating rather than proof that something broke. A close below $365 would most likely mean the market had stopped believing the FY27/FY30 framework: a Q4 FY26 miss or FY27 guide cut in December, a Design IP shortfall that echoes the 2025 miss (with the class action live, response due 2026-11-04), a new US export-control hit to China EDA sales, or clear evidence that AI agents compress EDA pricing.

Whether agentic AI expands EDA consumption (management's view) or compresses seat-based pricing
Durability of AI/semiconductor capex, which drives design starts and IP demand

The multiple: SNPS at ~26x versus CDNS at ~40x+. The gap could close or widen depending on execution and leverage (~$10B gross debt)
Size of non-GAAP adjustments (SBC ~$970M plus Ansys amortization); GAAP EPS is less than half of non-GAAP

Rate path: the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and the median dot shows no cuts in 2027, with the 10-year near 5%. Further hikes would compress long-duration software multiples, though fixed-rate debt shields EPS
reasoning: Round 2 revision. Round-1 facts from primary documents still stand (Q3 FY26 8-K/10-Q: revenue $2.477B, non-GAAP EPS $3.91, backlog $10.9B with ~49% due in 12 months, debt $10.04B and cash $3.61B, 191.6M shares; Investor Day FY27 guide of $11.10-11.20B revenue, $19.04-19.12 non-GAAP EPS, GAAP $8.16-8.61, SBC ~$970M, ~$3.1B FCF, mid-20s EPS CAGR to FY30, ~$1B buyback). Following the supervisor, I verified: (a) the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, with a 4.1% median dot at end-2026 and end-2027 (Chase summary; the CNBC page was blocked), and the 10-year averaged 4.99% in September vs 4.12% a year earlier (Alpha Vantage/Treasury data); (b) BofA's $600 target, FY27 EPS +7%, FY28 EPS +16% and 23% CAGR, plus KeyBanc's $605, now read directly on 24/7 Wall St, not from a search snippet; (c) from the 10-Q: China was $707M of $7.16B 9M revenue (9.9%), the class-action response is due 2026-11-04, and debt principal is ~$1.02B in each of FY27 and FY28. A primary-document point the supervisor did not make: the floating-rate Ansys term loans were fully repaid in Q1 FY26, so the hike hits the multiple, not EPS. Changes: every multiple is cut about one turn (P/E 24x to 23x, FCF yield 3.6% to 3.8%, SBC-burdened 29x to 28x), and fair value falls from $547 to $523 (+6.6%). The bear case moves from $370 to $355 and from 25% to 27% probability (fatter left tail for rates, Kimi-type AI scares and IP credibility), and the base case from $545 to $525. The scenario-weighted mean is ~$510. Following the supervisor's prompt on the median: given the documented de-rating (~40x to ~26x forward), a rising-rate regime and the fact that guidance-led jumps often partly reverse, I put the median at ~$500-505 (P(>=$491) 0.54, down from 0.56), below both fair value and the mean. The shape is roughly lognormal with ~39% vol (up from 38% because of rate risk), a slightly fatter left tail and a trimmed right tail (above $860 needs more than 35x earnings with a 5% 10-year). On the supervisor's findings: I agree with all the facts. I lower my thesis break to $365, but on my own reasoning, not to match its number. My fair value ($523) sits below its $540 because I apply the rate backdrop to all three methods. Research limits: CNBC, FRED and ETF Trends blocked fetching, so rates come from Chase and Alpha Vantage. Lane share is ~56% primary because the macro sources added this round are outside the lane.
